correctness.rationale: The four-dimensional cubic system follows from the surjective polar restriction with one-dimensional determinant kernel, the transverse complete-intersection ideal of nine basepoints, and the symmetric tensor product. The set-theoretic base is characterized by a symmetric product of two evaluation vectors. At rank-two pair intersections the completed ideal is (ux,uy+vx,vy), whose radical quotient is one-dimensional and killed by the maximal ideal; other rank-two points are reduced. At rank-one points, invariant-ring coordinates give the reduced plane quotient. A standalone symbolic check corroborates the critical socle identities; no finite test substitutes for the proof.
